name: Fork Union
workload: N-body parallel-for dispatch latency (512 bodies, all cores) and connected-components GTEPS on a 27M-edge graph, on Apple M5 Pro, Intel RPL, Intel SPR and AWS Graviton 5.
claimed_speedup: README headline: ~3-6x faster than OpenMP and ~12-16x faster than Rayon and Taskflow per parallel-for dispatch. Table row 128x Intel SPR n-body: ForkUnion C++ 54/86 us, OpenMP 115/226, Rayon 483/739, Taskflow 666/694. Connected components 192x Graviton 5: ForkUnion Rust 258.7 GTEPS vs OpenMP 53.9, Rayon 8.4.
hardware: 18x Apple M5 Pro, 24x Intel RPL, 128x Intel SPR, 192x AWS Graviton 5 (exact CPU SKUs not named)
tradeoffs: Fork-join data-parallel loops, not general dynamic work stealing; spin-based workers with NUMA-aware compute domains; no allocations, syscalls or CAS on hot path. Targets OpenMP-style parallel-for rather than recursive tasks.
caveats: Benchmark files scripts/nbody.{cpp,rs,zig} and scripts/propagation.{cpp,rs,zig} are public, but CPU labels are coarse (core counts and families, not SKUs). Latency win is dispatch overhead; throughput wins are smaller and OpenMP wins some cells (24x Intel RPL connected components 11.4 vs 10.0 GTEPS). Author-run numbers. Opened README only; did not open the script files.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'thread pool work stealing faster than TBB Rayon benchmark github' (Fork Union snippets)

name: citor
baseline: oneTBB, OpenMP (also BS::thread_pool, dp::thread_pool, Taskflow, Eigen::ThreadPool, dispenso, libfork, TooManyCooks)
workload: Sub-microsecond fan-out dispatch, parallel-for, reductions, scans and recursive fork-join across ten peer pools on Zen 5 9950X3D single CCD, plus Genoa and Sapphire Rapids validation.
claimed_speedup: No single headline multiplier in the README: 'wins majority of contested cells' on the single-CCD Zen 5 target; on multi-CCD hosts the win rate is lower and it loses stencil (to OpenMP), heavy-tailed reductions (to oneTBB) and some recursive fork-join. Charts in docs/charts.
compiler_and_flags: GCC 14 and Clang 19 on Linux, C++20, -pthread (full flags not read)
hardware: AMD Zen 5 9950X3D (taskset -c 0-15); AWS c7a.metal-48xl (Genoa), c7i.metal-24xl (Sapphire Rapids)
tradeoffs: Linux x86_64 focus, header-only C++20, Chase-Lev work stealing plus per-CCD arenas and done-epoch barriers; tuned for single-CCD CPUs.
caveats: README states results as chart shapes, not numbers; I did not open the per-chart data or benchmark/parallel_bench sources, so tier C. Author-run. Honest loss list is in the README.

name: chili
workload: Binary tree sum with fork-join on AMD Ryzen 7 4800HS and Apple M1 (8 cores each), tree sizes from 1,023 to 134M nodes.
claimed_speedup: Ryzen 4800HS, 134,217,727 nodes: baseline 797.5 ms, Rayon 497.2 ms, Chili 101.8 ms (about 4.9x vs Rayon, derived from page data). M1, 67,108,863 nodes: Rayon 167.1 ms vs Chili 44.3 ms (3.8x, derived from page data). Small tree 1,023 nodes: Rayon 51.1 us vs Chili 3.4 us on Ryzen (derived 15x).
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 4800HS (8 cores); Apple M1 (8 cores)
tradeoffs: Heartbeat-style join primitive (port of Spice), almost identical API to rayon::join; no parallel iterators or full pool features.
caveats: First-party README table, build flags unstated and benchmark code location not verified. README's own 'Improvement' column prints 0.53x for small trees, ratios here are derived. Last commit about 17 months before today.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'Rust fork-join parallelism library faster than rayon chili spice'

name: Spice
workload: Binary tree summation fork-join (100M nodes) at up to 16 threads, and a 1000-node small tree, versus a Zig sequential baseline and Rayon on the same algorithm.
claimed_speedup: Spice overhead under 1 ns per node vs sequential 7.48 ns; Rayon baseline 22.99 ns per node with about 15 ns overhead. Speedup at 16 threads: Spice about 11x vs Rayon about 14x relative to each own baseline (so not faster in scaling, faster in absolute time). Small tree: Rayon about 60x slower at 32 threads on 16 cores while Spice disables parallelism.
tradeoffs: Heartbeat scheduling (work shared every ~100 us), fork/join only, Zig API.
caveats: Rayon speedup on the same tree is higher than Spice's (14x vs 11x); the win is low per-task overhead and small-input behaviour. Build flags and CPU model not stated beyond the instance type. Zig, so not directly usable from C++ except via C ABI wrappers.

name: nexus
workload: Single-producer fire-and-forget, submit-and-get, recursive fork-join leaf tasks, 8x multi-producer, and round-trip latency, with 8 workers.
claimed_speedup: Recursive fork-join 28.40 M leaf tasks/s vs Taskflow 8.62 and BS::thread_pool 1.23; fire-and-forget 8.39 vs 1.24 and 0.40 M tasks/s; round-trip P50/P99 0.44/0.87 us vs Taskflow 2.66/7.44 us.
compiler_and_flags: GCC 16.2.1, Release (exact flags not stated), C++26
tradeoffs: C++26 and GCC 16.2+ required; header-only, work stealing plus lock-free MPMC, P2300 scheduler compatible.
caveats: Baselines are Taskflow and BS::thread_pool, not TBB, OpenMP or Rayon; no oneTBB row despite earlier search snippet mentioning it. First-party, best of three runs, README only (Chinese). Very new project.

name: ThunderBolt-HT
workload: Per-task scheduling cost via granularity regression (fixed work split into more tasks), partitioned parallel_for throughput, and a game-simulation frame graph, 20 interleaved repetitions median.
claimed_speedup: Per-task cost 286 ns vs Taskflow explicit tasks 451 ns (about 1.6x, derived from page data); earlier run 597-633 ns vs 643 ns. Partitioned parallel_for claimed to beat taskflow_for_each at every task count; full simulation gain smaller (stress 0.195 vs 0.206).
compiler_and_flags: C++20, toolset pinned in CMakePresets.json (not read)
tradeoffs: Dependency-aware task runtime with priority deques; mobile-class hardware with clock drift, authors use interleaved A/B.
caveats: Baseline is Taskflow, not TBB, OpenMP or Rayon. Laptop CPU model unstated. Self-reported, README only; result JSONs in docs/results not opened.

name: runtime-benchmarks (tzcnt)
baseline: oneTBB, Taskflow (OpenMP and Rayon not included)
workload: Cross-runtime fork-join suite: skynet, nqueens, fib(39), matmul(2048) on 64 cores, ten C++ runtimes.
claimed_speedup: libfork skynet 36,519 us, nqueens 69,010 us, fib(39) 62,367 us, matmul(2048) 44,140 us; oneTBB and Taskflow showed mean ratios of 3.25x and 3.34x versus the best performer.
tradeoffs: Benchmark suite only; winners are libfork and TooManyCooks (both already catalogued), citor is listed too.
caveats: Evidence for known projects (libfork, TooManyCooks) and for citor. Page says a LICENSE file exists but SPDX not read; last commit date not shown. Maintained by the TooManyCooks author, so not fully independent.
